The Randolph plan includes provision for studying the noise problem on some of these affected buildings, such as the West End School, once the Expressway is operating.
(5) Attentuation Measures: Bolt, Beranek and Newman has evaluated what effect incorporating a shielding barrier along Grayland Avenue would have on the noise levels of the site. The barrier considered consisted of an earth berm possibly topped by a wall in order to reduce the lateral extent of earth required. Although a continuous shielding barrier would be quite effective in reducing noise levels, it is not feasible for Randolph because penetrations and interruptions are necessary for streets and existing buildings in the area which must remain. Due to this fact, three various sized barriers, with interruptions for northsouth streets and buildings which are required to remain, were evaluated. A 20-foot barrier proved quite effective in reducing noise levels, particularly in areas where the barrier extended for a full block without interruption. A 15-foot barrier also substantially reduced the noise levels, though the Normally Unacceptable area was somewhat larger than the 20-foot barrier. Finally, a 10-foot barrier was assumed revealing that a 10-foot barrier would have a greatly reduced effect. Therefore this height of barrier was eliminated from further consideration.
Various structural remedial measures have also been considered in relation to interior noise levels of impacted buildings. For those buildings within the shaded areas exposed to 65 dBA through 70 dBA for more than 8 hours daily, the following treatment is recommended:
(a) Air-conditioning (so that windows need not be opened).
(b) Replacement of all openable windows with fixed glazing.
(c) Provision of exterior doors, to be 1-3/4" solid core wood with air tight gasketing or weather-stripping.
